newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia FDI rises to $83.1 mln in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia FDI rises to $83.1 mln in first quarter.

text.p: Foreign direct investment (FDI) in Slovenia rose to $83.1 million in the first quarter of the year from $22.4 million in the same period of 1996, the government's top economic institute said on Wednesday.

The Institute of Macroeconomic Analysis and Development said in its latest report this year's FDI was expected to grow significantly from last year's $185.9 million, but declined to give further details.

It said one of the largest single investments this year would be made by Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. which announced last month it would take a 60 percent stake in Slovenian tire maker Sava and a 75 percent stake in its engineering products business.
Sava is among the ten largest Slovenian companies. The purchase price has not yet been announced.

"A comparison of Slovenia with developed Western countries and most successfull countries in transition shows that FDI has a small role in the Slovenian economy if measured by its part in GDP," the institute said.
In 1996 foreign direct investment represented about one percent of GDP.

The institute added that although companies with foreign investment employ only six percent of employees in Slovenia's business sector they produce 15.3 percent of all profits and 20.1 percent of exports in the sector. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
